title: IMPACT: Improving Motion Precision in Advanced Clinical brain Tumor imaging
summary:
The movement of patients during MRI examinations poses a considerable challenge for the radiologists performing the examinations and often impairs the diagnostic accuracy of the images captured. Wrong conclusions can be drawn from images with pronounced movement artifacts. 
For patients with suspected brain tumors, MRI examinations are crucial for the diagnosis and monitoring of therapy. The assessment of the tumor burden must be precise and reproducible. High quality MRI data sets are required to accurately capture tumor dimensions, as motion artifacts can obscure smaller tumors or parts of tumors. 
In order to combat motion artifacts without physically impairing patients (e.g. by rigidly fixing the head), a new motion correction technique has been developed. For the first time, this technique can record head movement exclusively with a camera that does not touch the head. In the past, this required so-called markers, which were attached to the patient's head. The goal of this study is to show that the newly developed system significantly improves the image quality of MRI scans in patients with brain tumors.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Suspected (baseline) or diagnosed (follow-up) primary or secondary brain tumors and indication for routine brain MRI.
Exclusion criteria:
- Pregnancy
- Patients with major contraindications to MR scanning (e.g. presence of implanted MRI-incompatible cardiac devices or insuline pumps). 
- Factors that may affect their ability to understand and provide informed consent
